candidates.explanation: Inferred without seeing the code. AuthService.register does not set a provider, so UsersService.create supplies the default, which should be AuthProvidersEnum.email. The login error shows the stored provider is 'google', so this default is probably wrong. It may use AuthProvidersEnum.google, or take a provider from the DTO that isn't email.

This builds the create payload for a self-registered user. If it spreads the DTO or passes a provider other than AuthProvidersEnum.email, the user is saved with the wrong provider. validateLogin then rejects the email login with needLoginViaProvider:google.

This check returns 422 needLoginViaProvider:${user.provider} when user.provider !== AuthProvidersEnum.email. It is less likely to be the cause, because it reports the stored provider rather than setting it. Look here only if the comparison uses the wrong enum member.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, set the provider to `createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`. Make sure AuthService.register does not pass or override the provider with anything other than AuthProvidersEnum.email.
